- AI is reshaping semiconductor scaling, making advanced packaging a critical technology for integrating compute, memory, and connectivity into next-generation systems.
- From HBM and chiplets to hybrid bonding and panel-level packaging, advanced packaging is helping overcome the performance, bandwidth, and efficiency challenges of the AI era.
- As a result, outsourced semiconductor assembly and test providers (OSATs) are moving beyond traditional assembly roles to become strategic enablers of next-generation AI systems.
- As packaging becomes a key competitive differentiator, collaboration among chipmakers, foundries, OSATs, and equipment providers is increasingly shaping the future of semiconductor innovation.


For decades, semiconductor progress followed a familiar formula: make transistors smaller, faster, and more energy efficient.


That formula still matters. But the[AI era](https://newsroom.lamresearch.com/the-ai-revolution-relies-on-advanced-packaging?blog=true) is changing the industry's definition of scaling.


[Advanced packaging](https://newsroom.lamresearch.com/semi-101-advanced-packaging-techniques?blog=true) has become one of the semiconductor industry's most important scaling technologies. As artificial intelligence drives demand for more compute, memory bandwidth, and energy efficiency, advanced packaging enables chipmakers to integrate multiple technologies into highly optimized systems that deliver greater performance than traditional approaches alone.


As a result, advanced packaging has moved from a supporting manufacturing function to one of the semiconductor industry's most important innovation engines.


That shift is also reshaping roles across the semiconductor ecosystem. Outsourced semiconductor assembly and test providers (OSATs), long associated primarily with assembly and test services, are increasingly helping customers navigate complex packaging architectures, heterogeneous integration, and manufacturing scale-up.


In the AI era, advanced packaging expertise is becoming a strategic capability rather than simply a manufacturing service.


### AI Is Driving a New Era of System-Level Design


AI has exposed new constraints in computing.


The performance of advanced AI systems depends not only on compute capability but also on how efficiently data moves between processors, memory, networking components, and accelerators.


The industry’s growing "memory wall," or the gap between computing performance and memory bandwidth, has become a critical challenge. At the same time, power consumption and thermal demands continue to rise.


Solving these problems requires a broader approach to innovation.


Instead of relying solely on large monolithic chips, semiconductor designers are increasingly combining specialized components into tightly integrated systems. Technologies such as chiplets,[high-bandwidth memory (HBM)](https://newsroom.lamresearch.com/high-bandwidth-memory-explained-semi-101?blog=true) , hybrid bonding, and 3D integration are creating new pathways for performance growth while improving flexibility and efficiency. Advanced packaging has become a key enabler of this shift.


In many ways, the industry's center of gravity is moving from chip design to system design.


### Turning Architectural Innovation into Manufacturing Reality


[New architectures](https://newsroom.lamresearch.com/learning-from-nand-3d-dram-transition-ai-era?blog=true) only matter if they can be manufactured at scale.


As advanced packaging technologies become more sophisticated, they require new materials, new process technologies, and increasingly precise manufacturing techniques. Packaging is becoming more front-end-like in its demands for process control, defect management, yield, and reliability.


That shift is also visible in equipment demand.


At Lam, we’ve been investing in advanced packaging for more than 15 years because we recognized early that future semiconductor scaling would increasingly depend on integration as much as transistor density. Today, our portfolio supports critical advanced packaging applications including HBM, TSV formation, hybrid bonding, wafer-to-wafer stacking, and[panel-level packaging](https://newsroom.lamresearch.com/panel-level-processing-advanced-semiconductor-packaging-semi-101?blog=true) .


Those investments are reflected in real-world adoption. Lam holds leading positions in key advanced packaging technologies, including electrochemical deposition and TSV etch. More than 500[SABRE® 3D](https://newsroom.lamresearch.com/blog-sabre-3d-advanced-packaging-interconnects?blog=true) systems have been shipped worldwide, and Lam technologies are deployed across leading foundries, memory manufacturers, and OSATs.


For AI applications in particular, Lam technologies help enable the TSV and plating processes underlying modern HBM architectures, which are critical to delivering the memory bandwidth required by today's most advanced AI systems.


### Why Semiconductor Ecosystem Collaboration Matters


No company can solve the AI scaling challenge alone.


Progress increasingly depends on collaboration among chipmakers, foundries, memory suppliers, equipment providers, materials companies, and research institutions. Many of the industry's most important advances are happening at the intersections of compute and memory, silicon and packaging, and design and manufacturing.


As AI architectures become increasingly dependent on advanced packaging, OSATs are taking on more strategic roles within the semiconductor ecosystem. Rather than serving solely as manufacturing partners, many are helping drive innovation in heterogeneous integration, chiplet assembly, and advanced packaging technologies that are essential to next-generation AI systems.


Lam’s position across logic, memory, foundry, and advanced packaging gives us a unique view into these converging challenges. We collaborate with customers and research organizations,[including imec](https://newsroom.lamresearch.com/lam-imec-3d-integration-dry-resist-ai-semiconductor-scaling?blog=true) and leading universities, to help accelerate the development and commercialization of next-generation packaging technologies.


### Looking Beyond the Wafer


As AI systems continue to grow in complexity, the industry is also exploring new manufacturing approaches.


One area attracting increasing attention is panel-level packaging, which could enable larger package formats and higher manufacturing productivity for future heterogeneous integration architectures.


To support this transition, Lam recently opened a dedicated[Panel Center of Excellence in Salzburg, Austria](https://newsroom.lamresearch.com/wafer-to-panel-lam-scaling-advanced-packaging-panel-level-processing?blog=true) , and continues to invest in panel-level processing technologies designed for next-generation packaging applications.


While adoption will take time, the direction is becoming increasingly clear: future AI systems will require both architectural and manufacturing innovation.


### The Future Will Be Defined by Integration


The next wave of AI progress will not be driven by transistor scaling alone.


It will depend on the industry’s ability to integrate more compute, memory, functionality, and intelligence into highly optimized systems. That challenge requires advances in architecture, manufacturing, and ecosystem collaboration.


At Lam Research, we believe advanced packaging is one of the semiconductor industry’s most important innovation platforms. Through more than 15 years of investment, industry-leading process technologies, strategic partnerships, and continued innovation in both wafer- and panel-level packaging, we are helping customers build the foundation for the next generation of AI computing.


***Chin Hock Toh** is director, Technical Program Management, Advanced Packaging, at Lam Research.*


### FAQ


**What is advanced packaging?**


Advanced packaging is the integration of multiple semiconductor components, such as logic, memory, and chiplets, into a single high-performance system using advanced interconnect and 3D integration technologies to improve performance, bandwidth, and power efficiency.[(Learn more.)](https://newsroom.lamresearch.com/what-is-advanced-packaging-semi-101?blog=true)


**Why is advanced packaging important for AI?**


AI workloads require enormous compute power and memory bandwidth. Advanced packaging helps improve performance, reduce power consumption, and overcome data-movement bottlenecks.


**What is heterogeneous integration?**


Heterogeneous integration combines multiple semiconductor technologies into a single package to achieve higher performance and greater design flexibility.


**What role does HBM play in AI?**


High-bandwidth memory provides the bandwidth required to feed modern AI accelerators with data efficiently.


**How is Lam Research contributing to advanced packaging?**


Lam develops manufacturing technologies supporting TSVs, HBM, hybrid bonding, wafer-level packaging, panel-level processing, and other advanced packaging applications.
